To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
p53 can repress LRP transcription through Y‐box of LRP promoter through interacting with YB‐ 1, and the p53‐YB‐1 interaction can facilitate p53‐induction repression of LRP transcription.
p53 can bind to the LRP promoter via YB‐1 and inhibit LRP expression, and this inhibition is reversed by HDAC2.
the p53 transcriptional repressor can suppress the expression of the LRP gene through binding to the Y‐Box binding protein 1 (YB‐1) in the LRP gene promoter.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of LRP by p53 and YB‐1 and their role in chemotherapy resistance.
the role of p53‐HDCA2 complex in the suppression of LRP gene expression.
the regulation of LRP in MCF‐ 7 breast tumor cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
p53 suppresses LRP expression through YB‐1 in MCF‐ 7 cells, and loss of p53 related suppression of LRP is a potential mechanism for LRP overexpression in tumor cells and chemotherapy resistance.

the p53 transcriptional repressor complexes can suppress LRP expression by interaction with YB1, but this suppression is lost when p53 function is lost or p53 is mutated, leading to LRP overexpression and drug resistance.
p53 suppresses LRP expression through Y‐B1 in the MFC‐7 breast tumor cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the loss of p53 function is a key event in the process of chemotherapy resistance in tumor cell lines.
p53 suppresses LRP expression through the interaction with YB1 and the p53-YB1-HDAC2 complex can bind to LRP promoter and inhibit LRP expression.

p53‐related repression of LRP expression is mediated through interaction with Y‐box binding proteins, and loss of p53 related‐repression of LRP expression may be a reason for chemotherapy resistance in breast tumor cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the p53 transcriptional repressor can suppress LRP expression through YB‐1 interaction.
the p53 suppresses LRP expression through Y‐Box binding protein 1 (YB‐1).

loss of p 53 -related suppression of L RP may be the reason that tumor cells become drug resistance and that inhibition of L RP expression by siRNA can facilitate drug induced apoptosis of tumor cells.
